phrases.text: Measure J asks the voters of this high school district whether to reorganize it into two new unified school districts.
Today, this district runs the high schools, while separate elementary districts run the schools up to grade 8.
Measure J needs a majority of the vote to pass.
One new district would cover one elementary district's area, and a second the rest of this district, each running every grade through grade 12.
This district and two elementary districts would be dissolved, while five small elementary districts would keep their own boards.
Voters would elect each new district's board at this election, and the new districts would start in the 2028-2029 school year.
The impartial analysis does not include a cost estimate for the measure.
Opponents say dissolving an elementary district that did not seek this ends local control, and elementary programs could be cut for high school priorities.
Supporters say students would get one continuous path from the earliest grades through graduation, and the plan won unanimous approval after years of study.
A yes vote is in favor of reorganizing this district into two new unified districts, dissolving it and two elementary districts.
A no vote is against the reorganization, so all three of today's districts would remain.
